sentences.text:
As per the report of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Hathras, opposite party No. 2 has been
sufficiently served, however, she is not represented.
Heard Shri Rajesh Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the appellant and learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State-respondents.

The instant criminal appeal has been filed by the appellants, namely, Pappu @ Awnesh @ Awlesh Kumar, Laturi and Yogesh @ Yogesh Kumar challenging the order dated 27.11.2022 passed by Chief Judicial Magistrate, Hathras, whereby they have been summoned to face the trial for the offence under Sections 376, 506 IPC and Section 3(1)(10) of SC/ST Act and order dated 29.8.2022 passed by the Special Judge SC/ST Act, Hathras, by which non-bailable warrants have been issued against them in Complaint Case No. 850 of 2012 (Jashoda Devi vs. Pappu @ Awnesh and others) under Sections 376, 506 IPC and Section 3(1)(10) of SC/ST Act, police station Sikandrarau, district Hathras.

sentences.text:
1 Learned counsel for the appellants while referring to the order of the Coordinate Bench of date 28.3.2018 passed in Application Under Section 482 Cr.P.C. No. 9901 of 2018 submits that by giving a wrong name to the appellant No. 1, complaint case No. 850 of 2012 was filed and the same was not in the knowledge of the appellant-Pappu @ Awnesh , as the appellant Pappu @ Awnesh is having his real name as Awlesh Kumar S/o Balveer Singh and he could not appear before the trial court,
because it was not certain that it is Awlesh Kumar, who has been summoned by the trial court,
however, the Coordinate Bench vide order dated 28.3.2018 directed him (Pappu @ Awnesh @
Awlesh Kumar) to appear before the trial court for the purpose of obtaining regular bail, and in this regard, appellant Awlesh Kumar had moved an application for surrender before the Special Court on 8.5.2018, on which the report was called from the concerned police station and the concerned police station submitted a report that no person in the name of Pappu @ Awnesh S/o Balveer Singh is residing in the village, however, a person in the name of Awlesh Kumar S/o Balveer Singh is residing.

It is further submitted that as it was not certain as to whether the appellant-Pappu @
Awnesh @ Awlesh Kumar has been summoned in the instant case, the appellant Awlesh Kumar could not appear before the Special Court.

However, it is by passing the order dated 29.8.2022 on an application moved by the complainant/victim pertaining to the identity of the appellant No. 1, the process of nonbailable warrant was issued against the appellant No. 1 Pappu @ Awnesh @ Awlesh Kumar and appellant No. 2 Laturi.
It is further submitted that one of the witness of the complainant, namely, Bhuvnesh Kumar Sharma had submitted an affidavit before the Special Court stating therein that he had never appeard before the Special Court, as a witness.

It is further submitted that the complainant/victim of the instant case has also filed an affidavit before the Special Court on 19.1.2023 stating that no incident of the nature, shown in the complaint, has ever occurred with her and similar affidavit has been filed by her husband, namely, Netrapal.

It is vehemently submitted that the above factual matrix would reveal that the incident pertaining to which the complaint was filed by the complainant is false, and thus, the impugned order dated 27.11.2012 has been passed in utter disregard to the real facts, and is liable to be set aside.
Learned

Additional Government Advocate on the other hand submits that the appellant No. 1 Pappu @ Awnesh @ Awlesh Kumar is an absconder and appellant No. 2, Laturi is not having any of the ground in his favor, as there was no confusion pertaining to his name and appellant No. 3 Yogesh @
Yogesh Kumar had secured bail after appearing/surrendering before the Special Court.

It is also submitted that at the stage of summoning only a prima facie case is required to be seen and there was ample material before the Special Court to have summoned the appellants to face the trial,
thus, there is no illegality in the impugned order.

So far as the submission pertaining to filing of affidavits by the complainant or his witnesses is concerned, the same would show that the complainant and witnesses have been won over by the accused persons/appellants.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is transpired that by passing the order dated 27.11.2012, the appellants were summoned to face trial by the Special Court Pappu Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125441878/
2 for committing offences under Sections 376, 506 IPC and Section 3(1)(10) of SC/ST Act.

sentences.text: For the next six years, this order was not challenged by any of the accused persons, however, it was in the year 2018 (after six years of the passing of the summoning order) the accused persons had chosen to challenge the summoning order as well as the complaint by filing the Application Under Section 482 Cr.P.C. No. 9901 of 2018 and vide order dated 28.3.2018 passed by a Coordinate Bench the prayer of the appellants/accused persons to quash the summoning order of the complaint was denied/refused, however, as a concession, the accused persons/appellants were directed to appear before the court below for the purpose of securing regular bail.

It is also reflected from the record that instead of moving an application for bail and of submitting himself to custody one of the appellant before this Court, namely, Pappu @ Awnesh @ Awlesh Kumar, had moved a surrender application mentioning therein that by passing the impugned summoning order accused Pappu @ Awnesh S/o of Balveer Singh was summoned, while the name of the appellant/accused is Awlesh Kumar S/o Balveer Singh, thus, a clear report be obtained from the concerned police station.
The application moved before the Special Court was also to the tune that a clear report be obtained from the concerned police station.

It is also reflected that the police in pursuance of the order of the Special Court passed on this application, had submitted a report that no person in the name of Pappu @ Awnesh S/o Balveer Singh is living in the village, while a person in the name of Awlesh Kumar S/o Balveer Singh is residing in the village.
It also appears to be an admitted fact that accused-appellant-Pappu @ Awnesh @ Awlesh Kumar, is the only son of his father and is not having any sibling.

It was on 29.8.2022, the Special Court had noticed the discrepancy in the name of one of the appellant, namely, Pappu @ Awnesh Kumar, and on an application along with affidavit filed by the complainant with regard to the fact that Awnesh Kumar and Awlesh Kumar are one and same person, issued non bailable warrants against him and other person,namely, Laturi.

Nothing has been brought on record, which may even prima facie reflect as to what had occurred between the dates, on which the surrender application was moved by the appellant Pappu @ Awnesh @ Awlesh Kumar, in the year 2018 and 29.8.2022, the date whereon the order pertaining to issuance of non bailable warrant against appellants Papu @ Awnesh @ Awlesh Kumar and laturi was passed by the trial court.

Thus, in the facts and circumstances of the case mentioned above, this Court is forced to believe that the appellants Laturi as well as Pappu @ Awnesh @ Awlesh Kumar, remained out of the reach of the Special Court deliberately since 2018, and now suddenly, after many years they had approached this Court by filing an appeal against the summoning order, which was passed wayback in 2012.

In the considered opinion of this Court, the duty of one of the appellant No. 1, namely, Pappu @ Awnesh @
Awlesh Kumar, was to surrender immediately before the Special Court in pursuance of the order of the Coordinate Bench of this Court dated 28.3.2018 passed in Application Under Section 482 Cr.P.C. No. 9901 of 2018, and instead of submitting himself to the custody of the Special Court, the appellant No. 1 Pappu @ Awnesh @ Awlesh Kumar has attempted to make his identity doubtful by moving an application before the Special Court pertaining to the discrepancy appearing with regard to his name and that appears to be a deliberate attempt on the part of the appellant No. 1, as he had approached this Court by filing Application Under Section 482 Cr.P.C. with the name of Pappu @
Awanesh.

sentences.text:
3 Thus, for the reasons mentioned herein before, I do not find any good ground, on the basis of which,
the summoning order that was passed wayback in the year 2012 may be quashed.

So far as the submission of the affidavits by the complainant and the witnesses, whose statements were recorded before the Special Court are concerned, the same are required to be dealt with by the Special Court in accordance with law and no opinion in this regard is necessary to be given by this Court in an appeal, which has been preferred against the summoning order of date 27.11.2022.

Having regard to all the facts and circumstances of the case, I do not find any good ground, on the basis of which, the summoning order dated 27.11.2012 may be quashed/set aside, and in the end result, the appeal appears to be devoid of merit and is dismissed as such.

However, it would always be open for the appellant(s) Pappu @ Awnesh @ Awlesh Kumar and Laturi to immediately appear before the Special Court for the purpose of securing bail in pursuance of the order passed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 28.3.2018 in Application Under Section 482 Cr.P.C. No. 9901 of 2018.
